Ui.Script:
-- ── The material palette ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- The six materials a page can be printed on, and the ink each one takes. The COLOURS are -- the reference's own data (its Fonts.xml l.27-42) and are quoted verbatim: a different -- number is a different look. Benilla-scoped names — see the header. BENILLA_MATERIAL_TEXT_COLOR_TABLE = { ["Default"] = {0.18, 0.12, 0.06}, ["Stone"] = {1.0, 1.0, 1.0}, ["Parchment"] = {0.18, 0.12, 0.06}, ["Marble"] = {0, 0, 0}, ["Silver"] = {0.12, 0.12, 0.12}, ["Bronze"] = {0.18, 0.12, 0.06} } BENILLA_MATERIAL_TITLETEXT_COLOR_TABLE = { ["Default"] = {0, 0, 0}, ["Stone"] = {0.93, 0.82, 0}, ["Parchment"] = {0, 0, 0}, ["Marble"] = {0.93, 0.82, 0}, ["Silver"] = {0.93, 0.82, 0}, ["Bronze"] = {0.93, 0.82, 0} } -- The page ink and the title ink for a material, under the reference's published name -- (its UIParent.lua l.1880-1888). Falls back to "Default" unless BOTH halves are known, so -- an unrecognised material never gets one table's colour and the other's default. function GetMaterialTextColors(material) local textColor = BENILLA_MATERIAL_TEXT_COLOR_TABLE[material] local titleColor = BENILLA_MATERIAL_TITLETEXT_COLOR_TABLE[material] if not (textColor and titleColor) then textColor = BENILLA_MATERIAL_TEXT_COLOR_TABLE["Default"] titleColor = BENILLA_MATERIAL_TITLETEXT_COLOR_TABLE["Default"] end return textColor, titleColor end
-- ── The reader's regions, by role ──────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- The four material corners are one SET: a page is either bare parchment (all four off) -- or dressed in a material, in which case each corner wears that material's own art. -- Naming the suffixes once is also what makes the art path a single expression. local MATERIAL_CORNERS = { "TopLeft", "TopRight", "BotLeft", "BotRight" }
-- Everything a fresh ITEM_TEXT_BEGIN clears away. At that point only the title is known, -- so only the title stays on screen — the page and all of its paging chrome go. local PAGE_CHROME = { "ItemTextScrollFrame", "ItemTextCurrentPage", "ItemTextStatusBar", "ItemTextPrevPageButton", "ItemTextNextPageButton", }
local function ShowOrHide(region, wanted) if wanted then region:Show() else region:Hide() end end
-- A page always HAS a material: the server may name none, and the frame's own art is -- already parchment, so that is what "none" means. local function PageMaterial() return ItemTextGetMaterial() or "Parchment" end
-- Dress the page's four corners in its material. Parchment IS the frame's own art, so -- parchment leaves the corners off and lets the bare frame show through; anything else -- lights all four and points each at its own slice of that material's art set. local function DressPage(material) if material == "Parchment" then for _, corner in ipairs(MATERIAL_CORNERS) do getglobal("ItemTextMaterial" .. corner):Hide() end return end local art = "Interface\\ItemTextFrame\\ItemText-" .. material .. "-" for _, corner in ipairs(MATERIAL_CORNERS) do local layer = getglobal("ItemTextMaterial" .. corner) layer:Show() layer:SetTexture(art .. corner) end end
-- Put the reader on screen. The panel manager is allowed to refuse (something -- native-center is holding the screen) — and then we are not reading after all, so the -- server has to be told, or the session stays open behind a window that never appeared. -- The reference makes the same check, on both of the paths that open this window. local function OpenReader(frame) ShowUIPanel(frame) if not frame:IsVisible() then CloseItemText() end end
-- ── The event flow ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── -- One function per event of the reference's flow: ItemTextFrame_OnLoad registers FLOW in -- order and ItemTextFrame_OnEvent dispatches into Handlers by name. (The reference states -- the same pairing twice — four RegisterEvent calls, then a four-arm `if event == …` -- chain — which is how a fifth event gets added to one of them and not the other.) local FLOW = { "ITEM_TEXT_BEGIN", "ITEM_TEXT_TRANSLATION", "ITEM_TEXT_READY", "ITEM_TEXT_CLOSED", } local Handlers = {}
-- A text has been opened. Only its title is known yet, so the page is cleared away and -- the ink is set for the material the pages are going to arrive on. function Handlers.ITEM_TEXT_BEGIN(frame) ItemTextTitleText:SetText(ItemTextGetItem()) for _, name in ipairs(PAGE_CHROME) do getglobal(name):Hide() end local ink = GetMaterialTextColors(PageMaterial()) ItemTextPageText:SetTextColor(ink[1], ink[2], ink[3]) end
-- A foreign-language page is being translated: the turn buttons stand down and the -- progress bar takes over, ranged across the arg1 seconds the server quoted (OnUpdate -- fills it). Never fires on our letters — see the header. function Handlers.ITEM_TEXT_TRANSLATION(frame) ItemTextPrevPageButton:Hide() ItemTextNextPageButton:Hide() frame.translationElapsed = 0 ItemTextStatusBar:SetMinMaxValues(0, arg1) ItemTextStatusBar:Show() OpenReader(frame) end
-- A page has arrived. A letter signs off with its sender (ITEM_TEXT_FROM — the reference -- string really is comma'd); anything else just gets its trailing blank line. The paging -- row appears only when there is another page to be on, and then each button shows only -- if there is something in its direction. function Handlers.ITEM_TEXT_READY(frame) local creator = ItemTextGetCreator() local body = "\n" .. ItemTextGetText() if creator then body = body .. "\n\n" .. "From," .. "\n" .. creator .. "\n\n" else body = body .. "\n" end ItemTextPageText:SetText(body) ItemTextScrollFrame:Show()
local pageNumber = ItemTextGetPage() local hasNext = ItemTextHasNextPage() DressPage(PageMaterial()) if pageNumber > 1 or hasNext then ItemTextCurrentPage:SetText(pageNumber) ItemTextCurrentPage:Show() ShowOrHide(ItemTextPrevPageButton, pageNumber > 1) ShowOrHide(ItemTextNextPageButton, hasNext) end ItemTextStatusBar:Hide() OpenReader(frame) end
function Handlers.ITEM_TEXT_CLOSED(frame) HideUIPanel(frame) end
function ItemTextFrame_OnLoad() for _, event in ipairs(FLOW) do this:RegisterEvent(event) end end
function ItemTextFrame_OnEvent(event) local handler = Handlers[event] if handler then handler(this) end end
-- The translation bar's clock: while the bar is up it fills with the seconds spent so far. function ItemTextFrame_OnUpdate(elapsed) if not ItemTextStatusBar:IsVisible() then return end local spent = this.translationElapsed + elapsed ItemTextStatusBar:SetValue(spent) this.translationElapsed = spent end
-- Both page buttons are one gesture in two directions: the paging click, then the -- engine's own page request. `turnPage` is ItemTextPrevPage or ItemTextNextPage. function ItemTextFrame_TurnPage(turnPage) PlaySound("igMainMenuOptionCheckBoxOn") turnPage() end
